A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoVT research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, token and alignment ablations, training-stage experiments, runtime measurements, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds checkpoint-based baseline comparisons, representation-similarity results, and an attention case study.

M1.justification: The visual token types, expert alignment, losses, and four-stage training procedure remain unchanged. Although Section 3.3 changes the projection description from two fully connected layers to one, v1 Appendix A.1 already specifies the same single linear layer followed by cross-attention. This reconciles existing descriptions rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LLaVA-OneVision subsets, filtered TallyQA, ADE20K-Depth, and vision-centric and general benchmark suite. Appendix A.5 retains the dataset composition. The added attention example concerns counting visible letters within existing perceptual coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LVR and Monet to the existing Qwen2.5-VL, Claude-4-Sonnet, and GPT-4o comparisons, identifying reproduced checkpoint results. The Aurora comparison in Table 3 and the text-only and empty-token controls remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New Section 4.6 introduces layerwise cosine-similarity measurements using mean-pooled and tokenwise aggregation, plus answer-to-image attention inspection. Section 4.1 also replaces its generic training schedule with configuration-specific schedules already present in v1 Table 6. This corrects reported settings without establishing that training was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Figures 8–9 add targeted analyses of visual grounding through representation similarity and an uppercase-letter-counting attention example. Existing token-count, alignment, training-stage, text-only reasoning, and runtime analyses remain, including those in the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new similarity averages aggregate representations or tokens and do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds results including CV-Bench scores of 77.2 for LVR and 75.7 for Monet, alongside the unchanged three-type CoVT score of 80.0. Their reported V* scores, 81.7 and 83.3, exceed that CoVT configuration's retained 78.0. Figures 8–9 add similarity trends and an attention example; matched pre-existing benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2, Equation 7 corrects T_i^sam = proj(T_i^sam) to T_i^sam = proj(T_i^seg), repairing the formal mapping from predicted segmentation tokens to SAM prompts. The remaining equations and derivations are retained, with no new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about compact continuous visual reasoning, perceptual grounding, interpretability, and benchmark improvements. Additional comparisons and diagnostics support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 newly interprets representation similarity as stronger visual grounding and greater agreement between intermediate reasoning and final answers. Attention coverage is used to explain the successful counting example. The appendix's computational-overhead discussion and limitations concerning expert coverage and fully interleaved reasoning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit code-repository link and identifies checkpoint-based reproductions in Table 2. It also reconciles the main-text projection and training-schedule descriptions with details already supplied in v1's appendix. These are access and documentation improvements, not newly established implementation changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of LVR and Monet. Table 1 adds these methods and the already-discussed Mirage, and replaces the 3D-awareness criterion with broader perception enhancement. A visualization-of-thought reference is also added. The overall positioning among tool-assisted, textual, and latent reasoning approaches remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and explanatory edits, updates author affiliations, expands related-work discussion, and adds Section 4.6. The main narrative, contribution list, section sequence, and supplementary organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a three-way comparison of textual, tool-assisted, and CoVT reasoning. Table 1 is widened and expanded, Table 2 gains comparator rows, and Figures 8–9 add diagnostic displays. Existing material is redistributed; appendix Figures 8–17 become Figures 10–19 without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens comparison with relevant latent-reasoning methods, adds grounding diagnostics, supplies a code pointer, and resolves inconsistencies between the main text and appendix. These are useful incremental gains while the original method, results, and limitations remain. The new diagnostics lack sampling details, and Table 1's Mirage citation differs from Section 2's, leaving some weaknesses in the additions.
